newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sabena loss weighs on Swissair.
newsitem.headline: Sabena loss weighs on Swissair.

text.p: First half losses at Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by Swissair, accounted for a large part of a 27 million Swiss franc loss at Swissair's associated companies.
Sabena has not yet reported first half results, but a Swissair spokesman said that a large part of the losses Swissair sustained from its associated companies came from Sabena.
In June Sabena's chief executive Paul Reutlinger, former head of marketing for Swissair, said the carrier's earnings to May were lagging company expectations due to a series of strikes in February.
Sabena had a 1995 consolidated loss before provisions of 530 million Belgian francs compared with a 1.23 billion franc loss in 1994.
The loss at Sabena countered an improvement in Swissair's financial results stemming from lower value adjustments for securities and foreign currencies.
In the first half of last year Swissair reported a loss of 6.0 million from its associated companies.
Swissair's financial income in the first half rose to 113 million from 104 million and financing costs fell to 112 million from 156 million.
The net financial result in the first half narrowed to 26 million francs from 58 million.
